overview.title: A shortlist candidate, not a lease-ready opportunity
overview.finding: The saved five-minute area contains about 1,400 estimated residents. Several separately identified coffee and café alternatives sit a short modelled walk away.
overview.implication: There is a neighbourhood audience to test, but a generic coffee offer has no demonstrated competitive gap.
overview.action: Keep negotiations conditional on a differentiated repeat-visit proposition, a workable unit and affordable actual terms.
overview.confidence: Conditional commercial judgement; sales and pedestrian flow are unmeasured.

customers.title: Most of the resident base sits beyond the immediate five-minute walk
customers.finding: The Census-based estimates grow from about 1,400 at five minutes to about 5,200 at ten and 11,600 at fifteen. These are overlapping totals.
customers.implication: The larger outer figure does not create an equally convenient daily customer base. A repeat-visit offer must earn the additional walk.
customers.action: Test a short-walk neighbourhood proposition first; use the outer catchment only where customers give a specific reason to visit.
customers.confidence: Limited: 2021 Census allocated to walking contours, not a present-day market survey.

customers.title: Daytime employment does not establish a morning queue
customers.finding: The saved BRES context contains about 1,000 employee jobs in its native statistical area; wider-area modelled household income is about £50,000.
customers.implication: Neither number identifies workers passing the door, office attendance or disposable coffee budgets. Premium pricing cannot be justified by this income figure.
customers.action: Interview nearby workers about break patterns and their actual route, then test the proposed basket against their usual purchase.
customers.confidence: Dated contextual indicators; no local spend or journey survey.

customers.title: Neighbourhood occasions are more useful than a demographic stereotype
customers.finding: The ten-minute household profile includes one-person households and households without a car.
customers.implication: These are reasons to test convenient repeat visits and an accessible social stop; they do not prove social demand, poverty or willingness to pay.
customers.action: Ask residents to choose between a fast coffee visit, food pairing and a seated catch-up. Select the layout only after a clear preference and usable plan.
customers.confidence: Census estimates; household traits are not buying behaviour.

competition.title: A coffee gap has not been established
competition.finding: The reviewed set separates one verified chain coffee offer, one coffee-named candidate, two café alternatives, one bakery alternative and one pub alternative. China Garden is excluded.
competition.implication: The bakery’s published chain menu creates a concrete value comparison. A higher basket needs product, service or food value that customers recognise.
competition.action: Audit Star Coffee first, then Costa and Wenzel’s at the intended trading times; compare menu, queue, seating and actual shop prices.
competition.confidence: Scope is a targeted relevant shortlist, not a complete competitor census.

competition.title: Differentiate by an occasion that is still missing
competition.finding: Existing evidence cannot verify a specialty-coffee, quiet seating, early opening or food-quality gap.
competition.implication: A plausible proposition is a neighbourhood coffee stop with one strong repeat-purchase reason, but no specific format has won the evidence test.
competition.action: Adopt a feature only when competitor visits and customer interviews reveal that it is valued and currently inconvenient to obtain.
competition.confidence: Proposition hypothesis; current offer quality and trading hours remain unresolved.

access.title: The station is nearby; passing trade remains a separate test
access.finding: The new pedestrian route model reaches the TfL Ruislip Manor station point in about three minutes from the recorded building point. Coffee alternatives also lie around Victoria Road.
access.implication: Transport proximity supports an access hypothesis, but the customer may reach an alternative without passing this frontage.
access.action: Walk the station approaches in both directions at 07:30–09:00 and lunchtime. Record which paths pass the shop, crossings, visibility and the detour to enter.
access.confidence: Modelled route to a station point; entrance, crossings and volumes not field-verified.

access.title: Compare the frontage with the Victoria Road alternatives
access.finding: This address is on Manor Way; the reviewed alternatives are on Victoria Road. The saved catchments and street map show their relative positions.
access.implication: A nearby location can lose convenience to a shop on the customer’s natural route. A lower rent could compensate, but actual terms are unknown.
access.action: Compare visibility, approach direction and stopping convenience on site; do not pay a prime-frontage rent on the strength of a radius count.
access.confidence: Geographic comparison, not a measured footfall ranking.

premises.title: The current takeaway offer does not establish café permission
premises.finding: China Garden’s own page advertises evening collection and delivery at 132 Manor Way. Government guidance distinguishes hot-food takeaway use from café/restaurant use.
premises.implication: Existing food service is not proof that a daytime seated café or the proposed operations can occupy the unit without further checks.
premises.action: Ask for the lawful-use evidence, planning decision notices and conditions; confirm the exact proposed coffee/food/seating use with Hillingdon before signing.
premises.confidence: Business-page observation plus national guidance; the exact unit’s lawful use remains unverified.

premises.title: Choose the format after the measured plan
premises.finding: No verified usable floor area, customer facilities or equipment/service layout is stored for this unit. An Article 4 area record is present, with scope unresolved.
premises.implication: A takeaway counter needs queue, wash-up and storage; a seated concept also needs viable circulation and facilities. Neither is automatically cheaper to fit out.
premises.action: Request a measured plan, electrical capacity, water/drainage, ventilation, accessibility, waste arrangements and landlord alteration consent. Cost the actual scheme before committing.
premises.confidence: Material unit evidence missing; an area designation is not an exact-use refusal.

economics.title: Use the local benchmark as context, not this shop’s rent
economics.finding: The saved PropertyData restaurant cohort reports £28 per sq ft per year on an NIA basis, with 20 properties and an average modelled annual quote of about £27,600.
economics.implication: It is a different-use cohort with unknown model date, radius units and price spread. It cannot price this unit or prove that £24,000 is fair.
economics.action: Replace the planning rent with the agent’s actual annual quote and compare a verified compatible floor area; keep service charge, rates and repair liability separate.
economics.confidence: Provider modelled quoting context, not achieved rent or a statistical valuation.

economics.title: A drinks-only business and a food-paired business need different volumes
economics.finding: The model separates customer-paid prices from net sales, stock margin, card fees, staff, owner time and occupancy overhead.
economics.implication: A low drink-only basket needs more transactions to cover the same rota and lease. The menu must earn its assumed basket rather than inherit it from a benchmark.
economics.action: Test real basket choices at the proposed price and replace every scenario input with the written lease, supplier quotes and a costed rota.
economics.confidence: Deterministic conditional model; no selected-property costs or sales are observed.

discovery.title: The existing food business gives no evidence of a morning coffee market
discovery.finding: The selected business advertises service from 17:00, while the proposed coffee shop depends on a different daytime occasion. The same address also sits a few modelled minutes from established coffee and bakery alternatives.
discovery.implication: The current food-business presence cannot validate morning customers or daytime café permission. Taking over food premises can therefore leave both demand and lawful use unresolved.
discovery.action: Make daytime frontage observation and exact-use confirmation conditions of the deal, before spending on a café fit-out.
discovery.confidence: The opening times are advertised, not observed; lawful use and morning flow remain unknown.

advantages: A real residential base within the saved short walking areas.
Modelled station access is about three minutes; useful for testing a convenience proposition.
concerns: No verified café-use permission or usable measured layout.
No measured morning flow, conversion or defensible competitive gap.
Actual rent, rates, fit-out and staffing requirements remain unknown.
